page: Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-64 is a compute-oriented virtual machine configured with 64 x86_64 vCPUs across 32 dedicated Intel physical cores, utilizing two hardware threads per core. The instance provides 128 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 2.0 GB per vCPU. CPU cache resources consist of 48 KB L1 data cache per core, 2 MB L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. The architecture includes hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support), Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions for tile and INT8 execution), AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic acceleration. This instance does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark measurements indicate strong multi-threaded execution capabilities across diverse workloads. The server achieves a Geekbench multi-core score of 18,694.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 69,148.07, supported by high scores in extended vector instructions (75,345.31) and encryption tests (60,373.85). In specialized functional benchmarks, the instance delivers top-tier performance in PassMark database operations (33,231.61) and Geekbench image processing (18,377.0), alongside strong Clang software compilation throughput (44,250.0). Matrix operations supported by Intel AMX enable competitive CPU-based LLM inference, reaching 228.78 prompt tokens per second on 7B parameter models.

Resource allocation tradeoffs are defined by the compute-heavy ratio and reliance on remote persistent storage. While cached memory read bandwidth is high at 4,457.66 GB/sec for small blocks, large uncached reads and writes settle into median performance bands. With high core density and dedicated CPU threads, the instance represents an efficient configuration for processing-bound tasks that do not require high memory-per-core allocations. Best-fit use cases include parallel software compilation, CI/CD pipelines, image transformation, static web serving fleets, and CPU-driven machine learning inference.
description: The Google Cloud Platform n4-highcpu-64 is a compute-focused virtual machine configured with 64 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs across 32 Intel physical cores and 128 GB of RAM, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Hardware acceleration features include a 260 MB L3 cache, AVX-512 with VNNI, Intel AMX extensions, and dedicated cryptographic instruction sets. The server contains no integrated GPUs or local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistence. Benchmark evaluation demonstrates strong multi-core compute capability, with top-tier results in database operations and image processing, accompanied by strong throughput in Clang software compilation, static web delivery, and low-parameter CPU inference. The hardware profile offers balanced cost efficiency for compute-dense scenarios that need heavy multi-threading without requiring high RAM footprints, making it suitable for continuous integration, code compilation, media processing, and batch compute workloads.
